title: Anthropic shares tank after IPO as the Nasdaq erases 2026 gains
content:
A bruising stock market sell-off gathered steam Friday, despite high hopes that Anthropic’s record-setting IPO a day earlier would revive sentiment around the flagging AI trade.
Instead, Friday’s downturn was led by Anthropic itself, whose shares were down more than 11% after rising 17% on its first day on the Nasdaq Composite.
The S&P 500 was trading nearly 2% lower as it headed for its worst losing week since April 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his “Liberation Day” tariffs, and is now 10% off from its most recent high, entering what’s known as “correction territory.”
Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was off more than 3% and officially erasing all its previous gains in 2026. Other major AI-related names such as CoreWeave, Nvidia and Oracle also sold off.
The six consecutive declining S&P 500 sessions mark the index’s longest losing streak since April 2024. A seventh losing day would make it the longest stretch since the pandemic slump in February 2020, according to Deutsche Bank.
For U.S. households relying on 401(k)s and pension funds for retirement, the downturn is especially unwelcome at a time when inflation continues to prove stubborn.
Given the importance the AI trade has played this year in propelling markets and economic growth writ large, its derailment over concerns about costs, debt, profitability and political risk could have broader implications.
Deepening worries about AI revenues tied to exports of advanced technology to China compounded Friday’s sell-off.

The Jensen Huang scandal pulling down Nvidia appeared to broaden Thursday, when a short-selling firm issued a report raising questions about whether Advanced Micro Devices, another chip giant, may also have had shipments to Asia diverted to mainland China.
Alongside the stock sell-off, there has been an increase in purchases of U.S. Treasury bonds — a sign that investors are seeing signs of weakening growth amid higher interest rates from the Federal Reserve and a stalling economy in China.
“The pressure is becoming increasingly widespread, and that’s been felt across other asset classes too,” Deutsche Bank managing director Jim Reid wrote in a note to clients Friday.
Kevin Gordon, head of macroeconomic strategy and research at Charles Schwab, told NBC News that markets are feeling particular pressure from an increasingly “hawkish” Federal Reserve that is signaling aggressive rate hikes in the face of unrelenting inflation.
“They’re signaling that they want to be aggressive in raising rates,” Gordon said. Combined with a weeks-long downturn among AI and tech stocks, “we have dual forces hitting the market.”
Gaurav Mallik, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Modera Wealth Management, called the recent sell-off “a garden-variety correction.”
But he noted that overall returns have still been respectable this year, “especially against a challenging backdrop of rising rates, persistent inflation and fears about an AI slowdown.”
But a prolonged downturn could begin to cut more deeply into economic growth.
“If you have enough of a protracted downturn, which we really haven’t had since 2007-2009 in terms of length and duration, that’s when you’d really start to worry,” he said.

report.summary: Anthropic shares fell 11% a day after a record IPO, leading a broad AI selloff that erased Nasdaq 2026 gains and pushed the S&P 500 into correction.
report.background: Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, held a record-setting IPO this week, widely seen as a bellwether for public-market appetite for AI companies. The offering priced amid a years-long AI trade that has powered U.S. equities and economic growth, but also growing skepticism about whether AI revenues can justify soaring valuations. Investors have been weighing high infrastructure costs, debt-financed data centers, uncertain profitability, and political risk—especially U.S. export controls on advanced chips to China. The Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance on inflation and rising interest rates have added pressure on high-growth tech stocks. Friday’s selloff followed a short-seller report questioning whether AMD shipments may have been diverted to China, deepening worries about AI revenue tied to exports. The market reaction tests whether the AI trade can sustain its leadership or whether the IPO marked a peak in enthusiasm.
key_points: Anthropic’s shares plunged more than 11% Friday, reversing a 17% first-day gain from its record IPO. The reversal made Anthropic the epicenter of a market rout, showing how quickly investor sentiment can shift for even the most anticipated AI offering.

The selloff spread across AI names: Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave all fell, while the Nasdaq dropped over 3% and erased all 2026 gains. The S&P 500 fell nearly 2%, entering correction territory and marking its longest losing streak since April 2024.

Investors are worried about AI costs, debt, profitability and political risk. A short-seller report on AMD’s China shipments compounded fears about AI revenue tied to exports, while rising Treasury bond purchases signaled weakening growth expectations.

The Federal Reserve’s hawkish signals on aggressive rate hikes are colliding with the AI downturn. Analysts call it a ‘garden-variety correction’ but warn a prolonged slump could cut into economic growth, especially with inflation still stubborn.
report.impact: The AI industry faces a tougher funding environment as public markets question valuations and profitability. A closed IPO window could push startups toward private capital, debt, or consolidation, and force cost discipline. Developers may see slower hiring, tighter API pricing, and shifting priorities toward revenue-generating products; open-source alternatives could gain attention. Regular users will still get AI features, but hype may cool as companies focus on sustainable business models. Retirement accounts tied to equities will feel the pinch. The broader risk is a feedback loop: if AI stocks keep falling, investment and consumer confidence could weaken, dragging on economic growth.
report.tools: To follow the AI market and try related models, watch Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s GPT, Meta’s Llama, and Mistral. Open-source projects like Hugging Face, Ollama for local inference, vLLM for serving, and LangChain for building applications are worth exploring. For market tracking, use Nasdaq and S&P 500 dashboards, and AI-focused ETFs such as BOTZ and AIQ.
